name: Eluge, the Shoreless Sea
description: Eluge's power and toughness are each equal to the number of Islands you control. Whenever Eluge enters or attacks, put a flood counter on target land. It's an Island in addition to its other types for as long as it has a flood counter on it. The first instant or sorcery spell you cast each turn costs {U} (or {1}) less to cast for each land you control with a flood counter on it.
assumptions: Rendered the enter-trigger and attack-trigger as two separate sentences since they route to distinct downstream node ids.
couldNotDerive: The mechanical meaning of 'flood' (what a flood counter actually does to the land) -- no labels registry entry for it.
The */* defining rule (power/toughness equal to Islands controlled) -- no scaler node ties P/T to a counted game-state fact.
The cost-reduction ability entirely (first instant/sorcery each turn costs less per flooded land) -- untranslated.
notes: Confirms two already-known, undocumented-here gaps rather than finding new ones: (1) CharacteristicDefining$ True (a */* power/toughness defined by a dynamic count, SCHEMA's own sensor role) has no handler -- same general shape as Beza's dynamic-comparison gap, though simpler (a count of your own permanents, not a cross-player comparison), so likely NOT the same 'needs a design decision' tier -- probably just an unimplemented CharacteristicDefining$/SetPower$/SetToughness$ handler using the existing scaler role, worth a small follow-up. (2) The S:ReduceCost cost-reduction ability (a second Mode$ ReduceCost on this card, same shape as Eddymurk Crab's) is dropped -- now surfaces honestly as an unmapped S:ReduceCost entry after this batch's silent-drop fix, previously would have vanished with zero trace. The two ChangesZone/Attacks 'enter or attacks, put a flood counter' triggers (Forge lists this ability TWICE -- once under ChangesZone with Secondary$ implied by the attack-trigger's own explicit Secondary$True flag -- to fire on either event) reconstructed correctly as two separate PutCounter effects, each with a target land and CounterType$ FLOOD; the counter type/game-state-changing side effect (FountainStatic granting the Island type) is chained via SubAbility$ DBEffect -> StaticAbilities$ FountainStatic, which is a nested continuous-effect-on-a-remembered-object shape the translator doesn't yet follow, so 'It's an Island...' half of the sentence isn't independently derivable from the given nodes either (not confirmed whether this is unmapped or silently dropped -- not chased down further this round).
